entry.name: mc.train~
entry.description: train~ generates a pulse signal whose period is specifiable in terms of milliseconds (see <~ for a method of making a pulse wave at a specified frequency). It also sends out a bang when going from 0 to 1, so it can be used as a metronome with a floating-point interval.

arguments.name: inter-pulse-interval
arguments.description: Sets the initial value for the inter-pulse interval in milliseconds. The default is 1000 ms. If a signal object is connected to this inlet, the corresponding initial argument value is ignored.

arguments.name: pulse-width
arguments.description: Sets the initial value for the pulse width. The default is 0.5. If a signal object is connected to this inlet, the corresponding initial argument value is ignored.

arguments.name: phase
arguments.description: Sets the initial value for the pulse phase. The default is 0. If a signal object is connected to this inlet, the corresponding initial argument value is ignored.

attributes.name: phase
attributes.digest: Phase Offset (0 - 1)
attributes.description: Sets the phase of the onset of the "on" portion of the pulse. A value of 0 places the "on" portion at the beginning of the interval, while other values (up to 1, which is the same as 0) delay the "on" portion by a fraction of the total inter-pulse interval. Signal inputs override this attribute value.

attributes.name: width
attributes.digest: Pulse Width (0 - 1)
attributes.description: Controls the pulse width or duty cycle. A value of 0 has the smallest "on" pulse size, while a value of 1 has the largest. A value of 0.5 makes a pulse with half the time at 1 and half the time at 0. Signal inputs override this attribute value.

messages.name: signal
messages.description: In left inlet: Specifies the period (time interval between pulse cycles), in milliseconds, of a pulse train sent out the left outlet.In middle inlet: Controls the pulse width or duty cycle. The signal values represent a fraction of the pulse interval that will be devoted to the "on" part of the pulse (signal value of 1). A value of 0 has the smallest "on" pulse size (usually a single sample), while a value of 1 has the largest (usually the entire interval except a single sample). A value of 0.5 makes a pulse with half the time at 1 and half the time at 0.In right inlet: Sets the phase of the onset of the "on" portion of the pulse. A value of 0 places the "on" portion at the beginning of the interval, while other values (up to 1, which is the same as 0) delay the "on" portion by a fraction of the total inter-pulse interval.
